decisive_items: a 6×8 mm non-solid structure on the ventricular aspect of the anterior tricuspid leaflet with a “finger-in-glove” blind-ended protrusion
internally empty with filamentous adherent elements (“garland-like”)
echogenicity matching adjacent tissue, bulging in systole and relaxing in diastole
response.rationale: The mass on the tricuspid leaflet with a finger-in-glove protrusion, garland-like filaments, and tissue-matching echogenicity is pathognomonic for papillary fibroelastoma. Other candidates lack specific support: R4 only cites smoking without neuromuscular symptoms; R3 lists atherosclerotic risk factors but no lesion-specific features; R5 is contradicted by negative blood cultures and absence of infection signs.

rejected.why: Only active smoking is cited; no clinical features of Lambert-Eaton syndrome are present.
Atherosclerotic risk factors are background, not the cause of the described cardiac mass.
Negative blood cultures and asymptomatic course argue against endocarditis.
